newsitem.title: USA: US, Panama plan formal talks on anti-drug center.
newsitem.headline: US, Panama plan formal talks on anti-drug center.

text.p: The United States said on Tuesday it would begin formal talks with Panama later this month on turning Howard Air Force Base in Panama into an international anti-drug centre with U.S. participation.

State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said the two governments had "identified sufficient areas of common interest" in a series of informal diplomatic exchanges since Panamanian President Ernesto Perez Balladares visited Washington in September 1995.

"Talks will begin during the month of July with a view to concluding agreements on the creation of an MCC (Multinational Counternarcotics Center) and the matter of U.S. participation," he said in a statement released late on Tuesday.
The United States will turn over control of the Panama Canal to Panama and withdraw all troops and bases, including Howard base, by Dec. 31, 1999, in accordance with bilateral canal treaties.

The meetings have involved Ambassador John Negroponte, special coordinator for the Panama bases negotiations, and Panamanian representative Jorge Ritter. Negroponte chairs a U.S. Interagency Working Group on Panama, which is reviewing a possible post-1999 U.S. presence in that country.

Balladares has said Panama would not enter into talks with the United States to negotiate a military presence in Panama in the next century, but Washington could keep Howard AFB at no cost for use as an anti-drug centre.

U.S. officials have previously said the anti-drug centre under consideration for Panama would have a military component, and that 80 percent of current U.S. flights out of Howard base are counter-drug flights.
